q: Weak acids are weak ____ that partially ionize only to a limited extent in water. 2024,2025,2026
e: Weak acids do not completely dissociate in water, so they act as weak electrolytes.

q: Autoionisation of water is a reaction between two water molecules yielding ____ and hydroxide ions. 2024,2025,2026
e: During autoionisation, two water molecules react to yield hydronium and hydroxide ions.

q: The dissociation constants of bases increase as the strength of the base ____. 2024,2025,2026
e: Stronger bases dissociate to a greater extent, leading to a higher base dissociation constant.

q: The acidity of a base is the number of molecules of a ____ acid that will neutralise one molecule of the base. 2024,2025,2026
e: Acidity of a base is measured by the number of monoprotic acid molecules required for neutralization.

q: Acids and bases differ greatly based on their ____. 2024,2025,2026
e: Acids and bases vary in their ability to ionize or dissociate, defining their relative strengths.

q: Strong bases are strong ____ that ionise completely in water. 2024,2025,2026
e: Strong bases dissociate completely into ions, making them strong electrolytes.

q: The pH of grapefruit juice with a hydrogen ion concentration of 6.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³ is ____. 2024,2025,2026
e: Calculated using $\text{pH} = -\log[\text{H}^+]$, $-\log(6.5 \times 10^{-4}) \approx 3.19$.

q: The basicity of sulphuric acid is two since each molecule can provide two ____. 2024,2025,2026
e: Sulphuric acid is dibasic because each molecule releases two $\text{H}^+$ ions in solution.

q: ____ is the conjugate base for the acid HF. 2024,2025,2026
e: When hydrofluoric acid (HF) donates a proton, it forms its conjugate base $\text{F}^-$.

q: Acids that donate a maximum of three protons are called ____ acids. 2024,2025,2026
e: Triprotic acids contain three replaceable hydrogen atoms per molecule.

q: A conjugate acid results from the ____ of a proton to a Bronsted-Lowry base. 2024,2025,2026
e: Adding a proton to a Brønsted-Lowry base forms its conjugate acid.

q: A strong acid will dissociate completely in water and has the ____ Ka value. 2024,2025,2026
e: Complete ionization of strong acids yields high concentrations of products, resulting in a large $K_a$.

q: Strong acids are strong ____ that completely ionise in water. 2024,2025,2026
e: Complete ionisation allows strong acids to conduct electricity efficiently as strong electrolytes.

q: pH of of 0.01M HCl solution is ____. 2024,2025,2026
Water can also dissociate into hydrogen and hydroxide ions, and the process is known as ____. 2024,2025,2026
e: The self-ionization of water molecules into $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{OH}^-$ ions is termed autoionisation.

q: NH3 is a weak base and its ____ acid NH4+ ion is a strong acid. 2024,2025,2026
e: The ammonium ion ($\text{NH}_4^+$) is the conjugate acid of the weak base ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$).

q: The number of hydrogen ions that one molecule of acid can produce is the ____ of the acid. 2024,2025,2026
e: Basicity indicates the total number of replaceable hydrogen ions per acid molecule.

q: Acids that donate two protons are called ____ acids. 2024,2025,2026
e: Acids capable of supplying two protons per molecule are designated as diprotic or dibasic.

q: The capacity of water to function as an acid or a base is one of its ____ characteristics. 2024,2025,2026
e: Water exhibits amphoteric behavior, which is one of its primary unique chemical traits.

q: Lewis acid is a substance that can accept a (an) ____. 2024,2025,2026
e: According to Lewis theory, an acid is defined as an electron pair acceptor.
